question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Sarah said that she hates it when people ______ at her.
solution:
The correct answer is 'stare'.
 
Key Points
  • The verb "stare" means to look at someone with a fixed gaze, often for a prolonged period, which fits the context of the sentence perfectly.
  • The other options do not fit in this context:
    • Star – noun, referring to a celestial body or a famous person, not applicable here.
    • Steer – verb, meaning to guide or control something, unrelated to the action of looking.
    • Stair – noun, referring to a step or series of steps, does not fit the context.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.
 
Complete Sentence: Sarah said that she hates it when people stare at her.
 
Additional Information
  • Stare refers to looking at something or someone with a fixed or intense gaze.
  • In this context, "stare" is used to describe an uncomfortable or intrusive action of looking at someone for an extended period.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She is ________ of spiders.
solution:
The correct answer is 'afraid'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "afraid" means feeling fear or anxiety. (डरा हुआ)
  • The sentence implies that the person has a fear of spiders, making "afraid" the most suitable option.
  • The other options: "interest," "fear," and "frightening" do not fit the grammatical context as appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Complete Sentence: She is afraid of spiders.

Additional Information
  • Interest (रुचि): refers to curiosity or attention toward something.
  • Fear (डर): refers to an emotion of being scared, but it doesn't fit grammatically in this context.
  • Frightening (डरावना): refers to something that causes fear, but it is an adjective and doesn't suit the blank.

question:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

Rohan ordered his sister to shut the door before she left.
options: Rohan said to his sister, "Shut the door before you leave."
Rohan said, "Sister, shut the door before you leave."
Rohan said to his sister, "Sister, shut the door before you left."
Rohan said, "Shut the door before you leave."
solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. Rohan said to his sister, "Shut the door before you leave."

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in Indirect Speech. As per the given directions, we have to change it into Direct Speech.
  • As we have to transform the given sentence into an imperative sentence, the process of transformation is as follows:
  • The preposition 'to' will be removed and comma and inverted commas will be added.
  • In the direct speech 'ordered' will be changed into 'said to' because reporting verb has an object, 'his sister.'
  • The direct speech will begin like 'Rohan said to his sister.'
  • Now, let's focus on the reported speech.
  • The pronoun 'she' will be changed into 'you.'
  • 'shut the door' will remain the same in Direct speech.
  • Finally, the result is: Rohan said to his sister, "Shut the door before you leave."
  • ​So, the correct answer is option 1.

 

Correct Sentence: Rohan said to his sister, "Shut the door before you leave."

question:

This is one trip whom I will never forget.
solution:

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.

  • We know that 'whom' is used instead of ‘who’ as the object of a verb or preposition. [जिसे, जिसको (पूर्वसर्ग या किसी के कर्म के रूप में ‘who’ के स्‍थान पर प्रयुक्त)]

    • Example: She told me that she was leaving.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 4.
     

Correct Sentence: This is one trip that I will never forget.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The hunchback was being laughed at by everyone
options: Everyone is laughing at the hunchback
Everyone was laughing at the hunchback.
solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. Everyone was laughing at the hunchback.

 

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes subject performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the passive voice and 'The hunchback' is the subject and 'everyone' is the object.
  • When we convert this sentence into active voice, the subject 'The hunchback' of the passive voice becomes the object, the object 'everyone' becomes the subject.
  • The passive format "was + being + V3" is used and the active format "was + ing" should be used.
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the past continuous tense.
  • Hence, "Everyone was laughing at the hunchback" is the correct active voice.


 

  • Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:
     
    TENSE ACTIVE PASSIVE PASSIVE CONVERSION
    Present Simple He plays football am/is/are + V3 Football is played by him
    Present Continuous He is playing football am/is/are + being +V3 Football is being played by him
    Present Perfect He has played football Has/have + been+ V3 Football has been played by him
    Present Perfect Continuous He has been playing football Not used and unusual. Not used and unusual
    Past Simple He played football Was/were + V3 Football was played by him
    Past Continuous He was playing football Was/were + being + V3 Football was being played by him
    Past Perfect He had played football Had + been + V3 Football had been played by him
    Past Perfect Continuous He had been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Simple He will play football Will + be + V3 Football will be played by him
    Future Continuous He will be playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Perfect He will have played football Will have been + V3 Football will have been played by him
    Future Perfect Continuous He will have been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual

question:
Direction: Choose the option that is the indirect form of the sentence.

The hostel warden said to the inspector, “Aditya arrived on Sunday from the holiday.”
options: The hostel warden told the inspector that Aditya will arrive on Sunday from the holiday.
The hostel warden told the inspector that Aditya has arrived on Sunday from the holiday
The hostel warden told the inspector that Aditya had arrived on Sunday from the holiday.
The hostel warden told the inspector that Aditya is going to arrive on Sunday from the holiday.
solution:
The correct answer is "The hostel warden told the inspector that Aditya had arrived on Sunday from the holiday."

Key Points

  •  When the reporting speech is in Simple Past Tense then all the speech Changes to Past Perfect tense.
    • ​Arrived ------ Had arrived
  • 'Said to' of the reporting verb changed into 'told.'
  • Replace comma (,) and inverted commas (" ") with the conjunction 'that'.
  • The third person of the reporting speech remains unchanged.

Thus, the final sentence is: The hostel warden told the inspector that Aditya had arrived on Sunday from the holiday.
Additional Information

  •  Definition of Direct & Indirect Speech?
  • Direct speech – reporting the message of the speaker in the exact words as spoken by him.
  • Direct speech example: Mohan said, "I am eating now".
  • Indirect speech: reporting the message of the speaker in our own words
  • Indirect speech example: Mohan said that he was eating then.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Hundred and fifty rupees seem a high price for this little vase.
solution:
The erroneous part is 'seem a high price'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'seems a high price' should be used instead of 'seem a high price'.
  • As per the subject-verb agreement rule, a singular entity should be followed by a singular helping verb.
  • 'Hundred and fifty rupees' is a singular subject.
  • Hence, 'seems' should be used. 
     

Correct Sentence: Hundred and fifty rupees seems a high price for this little vase.

question:
Identify the Part of Speech of the underlined expression.

Students should not while away their time in frivolous activities.
solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 i.e 'Verb'.
Key Points
  • The underlined word "while" is used as a verb in this context, meaning to spend or pass time in a leisurely manner.
  • Verbs are words that express actions, occurrences, or states of being. Here, "while" denotes an action of passing time.
  • In this context, "while away" is a phrasal verb, where "while" works as the main verb in the phrase.
  • Verbs often indicate what the subject of the sentence is doing, which is evident here as it describes the action "while away their time."
Therefore, the correct answer is- Option 2.
Additional Information
  • Adverb: An adverb modifies verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs. In this sentence, "while" is not modifying any word, so it cannot be classified as an adverb.
  • Conjunction: A conjunction joins words, phrases, or clauses. "While" can function as a conjunction in some contexts, but here it is not connecting any elements.
  • Pronoun: A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun. In this case, "while" is not replacing a noun, so it is not a pronoun.

question:

Hence, the correct answer is ‘Option 4’.

 Additional Information

  • Noun: Represents a place, person, thing, or idea. 
  • Example: “Monday is the start of the week.”
  • Verb: Shows an action or state of being. 
  • Example: “The week begins.”
  • Adjective: Describes a noun or pronoun. 
  • Example: “I have a busy Monday ahead.”

question:
Direction: In the following question, there is a related pair of words given. Each pair is followed by four other pairs of words.  Choose the correct pair from the options:

Bravery: Cowardice
solution:
The correct answer is 'Bleak: Bright​.'

Key Points

  • Let us see the meanings of the words given in the question- Bravery: Cowardice​​:
    • Bravery: actions that are brave. (वीरता, साहस, साहसी कार्य)
    • Cowardice: a lack of courage; behaviour that shows that you are afraid. (साहस का कमी; भीरुता, कायरता)
  • In the given pair, the antonym of 'Bravery' is 'Cowardice'.
  • Now, let us explore the meanings of the words from the option:
    • Contrary: completely different; opposite. (पूर्णतया भिन्‍न; विपरीत)
    • Dissimilar: not the same; different. (असदृश; विसदृश, भिन्‍न)
    • Reject: to refuse to accept somebody/something. (व्‍यकि्त या वस्‍तु को अस्‍वीकार करना (मानने से इनकार करना))
    • Refuse: to say or show that you do not want to do, give, or accept something. ((किसी बात को मानने, काम को करने से) इनकार करना या बात नामंज़ूर होना)
    • Consequence: something that happens or follows as a result of something else. (परिणाम, नतीजा, फल, प्रभाव)
    • Outcome​​: the result or effect of an action or an event. (किसी क्रिया या घटना का परिणाम या प्रभाव)
    • Bleak: bad; not encouraging or hopeful. (ख़राब, बुरी; निराशापूर्ण)
    • Bright: happy; cheerful. (प्रसन्‍नचित्त, प्रफुल्‍ल)
  • The antonym of Bleak is Bright.
  • Complete analogy: Bravery: Cowardice :: Bleak: Bright​​

 
Additional Information  

  • Let us see the synonyms of the given words:
    • Mundane: Ordinary
    • Serious: Significant

question:
Direction: In the following question, there is a related pair of words given. Each pair is followed by four other pairs of words.  Choose the correct pair from the options:

Captivity: Freedom
solution:
The correct answer is 'Bind: Release.'Key Points

  • Let us see the meanings of the words given in the question- Captivity: Freedom:
    • Captivity: the state of being kept in a place that you cannot escape from. (कै़द, बंदी-स्थिति)
    • Freedom: the state of not being held prisoner or controlled by somebody else. (स्‍वतंत्रता, आज़ादी; दूसरे की क़ैद या नियंत्रण से मुक्ति)
  • In the given pair Captivity: Freedom, the antonym of 'Captivity' is 'Freedom'.
  • Now, let us explore the meanings of the words from the option:
    • Demolish: to destroy something, for example a building. (गिरा देना, तोड़ देना, ध्वस्‍त कर देना)
    • Ruin: to damage something so badly that it loses all its value, pleasure, etc. (किसी चीज़ को तबाह कर देना, बरबाद कर देना (कि वह बिलकुल बेकार हो जाए))
    • Defray: provide money to pay (a cost or expense). (भुगतान करने के लिए धन प्रदान करना (लागत या व्यय)।
    • Spend: give (money) to pay for goods, services, or so as to benefit someone or something. (किसी को या किसी चीज़ को लाभ पहुँचाने के लिए माल, सेवाओं, या भुगतान करने के लिए (पैसा) देना।)
    • Bind: tie or fasten (something) tightly together. (एक साथ कसकर (कुछ) बांधना या बांधना)
    • Release: allow or enable to escape from confinement; set free. (व्‍यक्ति या वस्‍तु को (किसी से या कहीं से) मुक्त करना, जाने देना)
    • ​Capable: having the ability or qualities necessary to do something. (कुछ करने में सक्षम या समर्थ)
    • Competent: having the ability or skill needed for something. (सक्षम, योग्‍य)
  • The antonym of Bind is Release.
  • Complete analogy: Captivity: Freedom :: Bind: Release

Additional Information  

  • Let us see some more examples of analogies:
    • Blunt: Timid
    • Busy: Idle
